symptom: An access rule WHERE whose members all resolve passed check -p and exec and failed mx check (11.14.0, Production) with CE0161 "Error(s) in XPath constraint." at Access rule of entity: [Title = $x], [M.E_Kid = empty], [Title = '[%CurrentUser%]'], [Cnt = '5'], [Status = 'red'], [System.owner = '[%CurrentUser%]'] on an entity without owner, [E_Kid/M.Kid/Name = 'a'].
file: mdl/executor/validate_access_rule_xpath.go (new: accessRuleXPathFormViolations from ValidateGrantEntityAccess; grantResolver.xpathFormProblems from validate_grant_refs.go check()); test validate_access_rule_xpath_test.go
cause: #1472's grantResolver.xpathProblem only asked whether members resolve. The form rules the retrieve and widget slots had (MDL047, MDL-XPATH01, the System-member rule) were never called for the grant slot, and nothing anywhere typed a literal against its attribute.
insight: Measure with one entity + one access rule per constraint in ONE app: mxbuild attributes each CE0161 to 'Access rule of entity X', so 86 forms cost two 17-second mx checks instead of 86. The matrix overturned three guesses: an access rule takes NO variable at all ($currentUser included - the token is the spelling); any string literal on a DateTime builds ('abc' too) while a Boolean takes 'true'/'false' in any case but not 'yes'; a decimal literal on an Integer builds while '5' does not. Enumeration literals match value NAMES case-sensitively (the caption 'Green' fails, the key 'Grn' builds) - the opposite of member names, which mxbuild folds. Reuse was cheap because validateXPathAssociations and validateRetrieveConstraints take a []retrieveConstraintRef: a grant is a one-element slice. Run the form rules only once xpathProblem is clean - a standing CE1613 suppresses every CE0161. Left silent: tokens other than [%CurrentUser%] (a date token on an Integer is CE0161 too), attributes reached over a path, and a token on an association to a non-User entity.
